Environment setup and sample app integration
Console walkthrough: endpoints, usage, Optimize recommendations
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this account. Carlos from our eng team is here to do the SDK walkthrough. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jared Liu: Good morning, thanks Maya. We have Priya and Aisha on as well, we're excited to see the integration path.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll do a ~10 minute overview, then Carlos will demo Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns, and then open up for Q&A and next steps.
[00:25] Carlos Ortega: Hi all, Carlos here. I'll jump into code in a sec. Note, some of the CLI output might show slightly different model names in the demo environment, we saw some auto-transcribe issues last week.
[00:34] Priya Nair: Totally fine, we mainly want to know how to wire auth, env vars, and how Console ties in for monitoring.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Great, and on the roadmap side you mentioned potential Dedicated + VPC later, correct Jared?
[00:46] Jared Liu: Yeah, if costs and latency look good we'll move to Dedicated with VPC peering. Also SOC2 and KMS are must-haves.
[00:55] Carlos Ortega: Perfect, we'll cover KMS integrations and how to use secrets manager for API keys.
[01:02] [01:02] Carlos Ortega: Ok jumping into the Python quickstart. I'm going to open the repo we shared in the invite - link: github.com/redwood/quickstarts/solace-sample (note: demo link).
[01:12] Carlos Ortega: First step is pip install redwood-inference - pip will pull the SDK. Example code:
[01:18] Carlos Ortega: from redwood_inference import Client
[01:22] Carlos Ortega: client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
[01:27] Carlos Ortega: Then response = client.generate(model="redwood/fast-7b", prompt="...", max_tokens=256)
[01:33] Priya Nair: Quick question - do you recommend storing API keys in env vars or in a secrets manager? We use HashiCorp Vault.
[01:39] Carlos Ortega: Best practice is secrets manager and inject into runtime; env vars are fine for dev/local quickstarts. We have examples for Vault and AWS Secrets Manager in the repo. For Dedicated/Private we support KMS/HSM integration for envelope encryption.
[01:52] Aisha Khan: How does rotation work? We have strict rotation policies.
[01:56] Carlos Ortega: You can rotate keys in the console; for host integrations we advise using short-lived tokens from your identity provider and mapping those to Redwood API keys via our management API. There's a refresh token flow in the examples.
[02:08] [02:08] Maya Chen: Also note - for SSO customers we offer SAML/SCIM provisioning and RBAC, so you can tie API key permissions to roles. We'll send the SSO kit in the security pack.
[02:19] Tom (PM): Regarding auth - is there a way to scope keys to model or route level? We want to limit who can call a high-cost model.
[02:26] Carlos Ortega: Yes, you can create scoped keys tied to model aliases and enforce per-key quotas. It's in the console under API keys -> Create Key -> Scopes.
[02:34] [02:34] Carlos Ortega: Now TypeScript quickstart. npm install @redwood/inference, then init:
[02:39] Carlos Ortega: import { RedwoodClient } from "@redwood/inference"
[02:43] Carlos Ortega: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
[02:49] Carlos Ortega: const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: "redwood-chat-3b", messages: [...] })
[02:55] Priya Nair: Does the client support streaming? We stream tokens to web UI.
[02:59] Carlos Ortega: Yes - both SDKs support streaming via websocket or http chunked responses. There's a sample react component in the quickstart that wires a streaming socket into a UI. We demoed that.
[03:11] [03:11] Priya Nair: Any rate limit guidance for streaming?
[03:15] Carlos Ortega: We expose token/req limits in the plan; for Dedicated you can configure cluster-level autoscale to fit QPS. Console has per-route dashboards with token breakdown to help tune batching.
[03:25] Jared Liu: You mentioned batching - we do batched embeddings and reuse prefix caching. How much work to enable KV cache?
[03:33] Carlos Ortega: KV cache (sometimes in docs auto-transcribed as KV cash) is handled by the runtime when you use the 'cache=true' param or via our SDK cache client. For stateful chat you can pass cached KV in the request; the SDK has helpers to persist and reuse. For high throughput we recommend prefix caching combined with continuous batching.
[03:48] [03:48] Priya Nair: Ok. On networking: if we go VPC, what's required?
[03:52] Maya Chen: For Redwood Dedicated VPC we support VPC peering and customer-managed subnets; we can provide a network checklist. For Private on-prem we have an appliance that can run behind your firewall. We'll include the network requirements in the security pack.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: Does the Console show per-token cost? We want to allocate costs per team.
[04:09] Carlos Ortega: Yes, Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and you can tag requests by API key or route so billing can be mapped to teams.
[04:17] [04:17] Carlos Ortega: Now I'll run a live quick demo. I'll set REDWOOD_API_KEY locally and run the python sample to call a small model.
[04:24] Carlos Ortega: (typing) Okay running: python quickstart.py --prompt "What's the best way to do feature X?"
[04:31] [04:31] (terminal output)
[04:32] Carlos Ortega: Response came back at ~120ms for the small dev model; note this is the hosted dev cluster, production numbers will differ.
[04:40] Priya Nair: 120ms is promising for our interactive features. What's the production latency for 7B with 256 tokens?
[04:45] Carlos Ortega: Depends on hardware/profile; on our curated 7b profiles median p95 is ~220-350ms with proper batch config. We'll run your exact workload in the benchmark.
[04:55] [04:55] Jared Liu: About quality/regression - do you support evals/quality monitoring?
[04:59] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and can alert on regressions. We can link evaluations to rollouts so you don't accidentally change outputs in production.
[05:09] [05:09] Tom (PM): For the pilot we want a small integration in our checkout and an embeddings index for search, can you support both?
[05:15] Carlos Ortega: Absolutely - SDK supports chat/generation and embeddings. We have a sample that indexes product descriptions into embeddings and shows retrieval-augmented responses. We'll share that example.
[05:24] Priya Nair: For embeddings we need vector db integration. Do you have built connectors?
[05:28] Carlos Ortega: We have sample connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, and a simple open-source vector store in the quickstart. For Dedicated you can also run your vector store in the same VPC.
[05:36] [05:36] Aisha Khan: Security deep dive later - we need audit logs and key rotation details.
[05:41] Maya Chen: Noted, that will be in the security pack. We'll include example audit log formats and retention options.
[05:48] Carlos Ortega: Alright, wrapping up the code section - quick note on env setup: we recommend these env vars in CI/CD: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (dev/prod), REDWOOD_MODEL_ALIAS. For local dev use a .env file and the local token manager sample.
[06:05] Priya Nair: How do model rollouts work? We want canary and auto-fallback to smaller models on errors.
[06:10] Carlos Ortega: Console has rollout controls - you can route % traffic to a model variant, enable automatic fallback policies, and configure latency or error SLO-based failover.
[06:20] [06:20] Jared Liu: Cost controls - can we set hard caps?
[06:24] Maya Chen: Yes, per-key quotas and hard spend limits are supported. We'll also show you Optimize recommendations to reduce token spend, like quantized model suggestions and batching configs.
[06:35] Carlos Ortega: One more demo - I'll show the Console quickstart: route creation, API key scoping, and where to download the SDK snippets. (screen share)
[06:45] Carlos Ortega: Here's the quickstart panel - click 'create key', then 'scoped', choose models and routes. The SDK snippet inserts the key usage pattern - we copy that into the repo.
[06:55] [06:55] Priya Nair: That looks straightforward. Any gotchas for TypeScript builds and bundlers?
[06:59] Carlos Ortega: If you're using certain bundlers you may need to polyfill WebSocket, but the package doc covers that. For server-side Node it's seamless.
[07:07] [07:07] Jared Liu: Ok final: timeline - we want a pilot in 1 week if the benchmark looks good.
[07:12] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Carlos, you'll run the benchmark with their sample and we'll follow up with pilot plan and pricing.
[07:18] Carlos Ortega: Yep I'll kick off a 2k-req bench and send results.
[07:22] [07:22] Maya Chen: Any other questions?
[07:25] Priya Nair: One last: can we store logs in our S3?
[07:29] Maya Chen: Yes, we support log export to customer S3 buckets for Dedicated/Private and can stream logs to your SIEM. We'll include the config steps in the pack.
[07:39] Tom (PM): Thanks - can you also include estimated cost for the pilot?
[07:42] Maya Chen: We'll include pricing options for hosted vs Dedicated and expected token cost estimates.
[07:48] [07:48] Maya Chen: Alright wrapping up - recap: Maya to send security + pricing pack, Carlos to run benchmarks and share quickstart repo and benchmark script, Priya to send schema and QPS targets. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-06-21.
[07:59] [07:59] Jared Liu: Great thanks everyone.
[08:02] [08:02] End of meeting

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g. KV cache -> KV cash), speaker labels sometimes shortened, and code snippets trimmed for readability.
